name: Port closure / shipping disruption
description: A typhoon, strike or other disruption shuts a port our supplies pass through. Shipments from the affected suppliers cannot move until it reopens, so lead times stretch and freight rates rise. Pick a supplier country, or Penang Port itself, where all our imports land.
precedent: COVID-related shutdowns at Yantian port (Shenzhen) in 2021 delayed shipments for weeks.

China.name: Yantian Port (Shenzhen)
China.precedent: COVID-related shutdowns at Yantian port (Shenzhen) in 2021 delayed shipments for weeks.

Taiwan.name: Kaohsiung Port
Taiwan.precedent: Typhoon Krathon made landfall at Kaohsiung in October 2024 and temporarily shut Taiwan's major ports, including Kaohsiung.

South Korea.name: Busan Port
South Korea.precedent: Typhoon Hinnamnor closed Busan port in September 2022 and disrupted Asian shipping schedules.

Japan.name: Port of Kobe
Japan.precedent: Typhoon Jebi flooded container terminals at Kobe and Osaka in September 2018 and shut Kansai Airport.

Vietnam.name: Port of Haiphong
Vietnam.precedent: Super Typhoon Yagi closed Hai Phong's container terminals in September 2024; they took several days to reopen.

Malaysia.name: Penang Port
Malaysia.precedent: Penang Port has had no full closure on record. The nearest case: monsoon floods in November 2025 closed roads and disrupted container traffic around Port Klang.

name: Global electronics demand slump
description: End-market demand for electronics falls. Customers cut orders, so stock bought for the old plan piles up and cash is tied up in inventory.
precedent: The 2022-23 electronics and chip inventory glut after the pandemic demand boom.
